To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gravitino production is the dominant source of gravitino relic abundance for reheat temperatures above 10^10 GeV and for supersymmetry breaking scales below 10^11 GeV.

gravitino production in models with a large splitting between particle and particle masses is typically dominated by the decay of the inflaton and that the supersymmetry-breaking scale is bounded by the reheat temperature.

(a) Gravitinos produced from reheating in the MSSM can dominate over those from thermal production, and (b) Gravitino production from thermal interactions can dominate over that from reheating in Split Supersymmetry, unless the reheat temperature is very small, T_RH < 10^{5} GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of gravitinos from the decay of the inflaton in split supersymmetric models.
the production of gravitinos from reheating and their cosmological implications.
the production of gravitino dark matter in models of split supersymmetery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gravitino production in the split supersymmetric models is not a problem for the baryogenesis and dark matter, as long as the gravitino mass is below the electroweak scale.
the gravitino production is not negligible in the context of the split SUSY models, and it should not be ignored.
gravitinos produced from reheating are a potential source of problems for split supersymmetry models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of gravitinos from reheating is an interesting issue to be considered in split supersymmetric scenarios.
gravitino production in the context of reheating in split susy models is not as bad as one would naively expect.
gravitino production is an efficient mechanism for generating a cosmological abundance of gravitinos, which can be used for baryogenesis and/or dark matter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in the case of a low reheat temperature, the gravitino abundance is dominated by the production at the time of reheating, and the supersymmetry scale is typically lower than in the case of thermal production.

the gravitinos produced from the decay of the inflaton can be a dominant component of the thermal bath, and hence a significant source of dark matter in models of split supersymetry, and that the constraints on split supersymmetry from the gravitino abundance are weaker in these models.
the gravitino production in split supersymmetries is a generic feature and cannot be ignored in cosmological studies.
